title: Magic Quadrant — Gap Criteria Schema
description: Supplemental schema covering the 7 MQ evaluation criteria NOT adequately addressed by existing MDR capability or pricing schemas. Designed to be scored independently then combined with MDR data via the MQ scoring mode to produce final Ability-to-Execute and Completeness-of-Vision positions.
source_document: G00802987 — How Markets and Vendors Are Evaluated in Gartner Magic Quadrants (2 July 2025)

levels.0: No Evidence — No public data or documentation found
levels.1: Minimal — Vague or unsubstantiated claims only
levels.2: Basic — Some evidence but significant gaps remain
levels.3: Demonstrated — Clear evidence of capability with moderate depth
levels.4: Strong — Well-documented with multiple proof points
levels.5: Market-Leading — Best-in-class with extensive evidence and third-party validation

pillars.description: Assessment of the vendor's overall financial health, the financial and practical success of the relevant business unit, and the likelihood that the business will continue to invest in the product.

sub_pillars.description: Annual revenue (total and cybersecurity/MDR-specific where available), year-over-year growth rate, and revenue trend direction over last 3 years.

scoring_guidance.2: Revenue disclosed but flat or declining; or only total company revenue with no segment breakdown
scoring_guidance.3: Positive revenue growth documented; cybersecurity segment identifiable; growing customer base implied
scoring_guidance.4: Strong documented growth (>20% YoY) with specific cybersecurity/MDR revenue; clear growth trajectory
scoring_guidance.5: Market-leading revenue in MDR segment; sustained high growth; public financials with segment breakdowns

sub_pillars.description: Profitability indicators, burn rate (for startups), cash reserves, debt levels, and overall financial sustainability.

scoring_guidance.1: No financial health data available; high-risk funding stage with no recent rounds
scoring_guidance.2: Recent funding secured but high burn rate implied; or large company but MDR is a minor, unfunded initiative
scoring_guidance.3: Adequate financial runway (2+ years); stable parent company backing; or breakeven trajectory
scoring_guidance.4: Profitable or near-profitable; strong cash position; parent company with solid financials backing MDR investment
scoring_guidance.5: Profitable with strong margins; investment-grade parent; demonstrated commitment to sustained MDR R&D investment

sub_pillars.description: Published customer count, customer logos, net retention rate, churn indicators, and customer base growth.

scoring_guidance.1: No customer count or logos published
scoring_guidance.2: A few customer logos or case studies; no count or retention data
scoring_guidance.3: Published customer count (100+); multiple case studies across sectors; growth implied
scoring_guidance.4: Large customer base (500+); net retention data available; expansion revenue documented; diverse verticals
scoring_guidance.5: 1000+ customers; published NRR >110%; major enterprise logos; low churn documented

sub_pillars.description: Estimated market share, inclusion in analyst reports (MQ/Wave), competitive win rates, and brand recognition in the MDR market.

scoring_guidance.1: No analyst recognition or competitive positioning evidence
scoring_guidance.2: Mentioned in one analyst report or industry list
scoring_guidance.3: Included in multiple analyst reports; recognized in competitive comparisons; moderate brand recognition
scoring_guidance.4: Named in Gartner MQ/Forrester Wave; strong competitive positioning; well-known brand
scoring_guidance.5: Leader in Gartner MQ or Forrester Wave; top-3 market share; benchmark vendor in the market

pillars.description: The vendor's capabilities in presales/sales activities, channel strategy, and the structure that supports market reach.

sub_pillars.description: Direct sales vs. channel/reseller mix, MSSP partner program, technology alliance partnerships, marketplace presence.

scoring_guidance.1: No channel or partner information published
scoring_guidance.2: Direct sales only; minimal partner mentions
scoring_guidance.3: Documented partner program; some marketplace presence; mix of direct and channel
scoring_guidance.4: Mature partner program with tiered structure; 50+ partners; technology alliances; marketplace listings
scoring_guidance.5: Extensive global partner ecosystem; MSSP-first model; 100+ channel partners; deep technology alliance network

sub_pillars.description: Sales approach (product-led vs. sales-led), trial/POC availability, sales team presence, deal velocity indicators.

scoring_guidance.1: No sales motion evidence; contact-us only
scoring_guidance.2: Basic demo request form; no trial or POC program visible
scoring_guidance.3: Free trial or POC documented; sales team roles in job postings; demo process clear
scoring_guidance.4: Product-led growth with self-serve + enterprise sales; fast deal cycles documented; sales engineering team visible
scoring_guidance.5: Multi-motion sales (PLG + enterprise + channel); documented fast time-to-value; sales team in multiple regions

sub_pillars.description: Sales presence across regions, office locations, language capabilities for sales, and regional go-to-market teams.

scoring_guidance.2: HQ region plus one additional region; limited international
scoring_guidance.3: Sales presence in 2-3 major regions; some international partners
scoring_guidance.4: Sales teams in 4+ regions; multi-language sales support; regional partners in each major market
scoring_guidance.5: Global sales presence; offices in all major regions; localized sales motions; 20+ country coverage

sub_pillars.description: Evidence of efficient customer acquisition: lead generation, demand generation effectiveness, sales cycle optimization.

scoring_guidance.1: No evidence of structured demand generation
scoring_guidance.2: Basic website lead gen; limited content marketing
scoring_guidance.3: Structured demand gen with content, events, and digital presence; ROI calculators or assessment tools
scoring_guidance.4: Multi-channel demand gen; documented fast sales cycles; strong digital presence with conversion optimization
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class demand engine; documented CAC efficiency; industry-leading content velocity; community-driven growth

pillars.description: The vendor's ability to respond, change direction, be flexible and achieve competitive success as opportunities develop, competitors act, customer needs evolve and market dynamics change.

sub_pillars.description: Frequency and substance of product releases, feature updates, and platform improvements over the last 12-24 months.

scoring_guidance.1: No release history or changelog available
scoring_guidance.2: Infrequent updates; 1-2 releases per year with minor features
scoring_guidance.3: Regular release cadence (quarterly+); meaningful feature additions documented
scoring_guidance.4: Frequent releases (monthly+); major capability additions; clear acceleration of innovation
scoring_guidance.5: Continuous delivery; weekly/bi-weekly releases; rapid response to market changes; documented velocity metrics

sub_pillars.description: Evidence of the vendor adapting to competitive moves, market shifts, or emerging threats (e.g., adding AI capabilities, expanding to new segments).

scoring_guidance.2: Slow to respond; capabilities lag market trends by 12+ months
scoring_guidance.3: Demonstrates awareness of market trends; key capabilities added within 6-12 months of market demand
scoring_guidance.4: Proactive response to market shifts; early adopter of critical trends; documented competitive pivots
scoring_guidance.5: Market-shaping; consistently first to market with emerging capabilities; sets competitive agenda

sub_pillars.description: Recent acquisitions, strategic investments, or divestitures that demonstrate market responsiveness and growth strategy.

scoring_guidance.1: No acquisition or investment activity documented
scoring_guidance.2: Minimal M&A; 1 small acquisition in last 3 years
scoring_guidance.3: Strategic acquisitions that filled capability gaps; clear investment thesis
scoring_guidance.4: Multiple strategic acquisitions integrated successfully; strong M&A track record; capability-driven investment strategy
scoring_guidance.5: Transformative M&A strategy; major acquisitions that reshaped market position; integration excellence documented

sub_pillars.description: Evidence that the vendor incorporates customer feedback into product development and delivers on customer-requested features.

scoring_guidance.2: Basic feedback collection but no evidence of incorporation
scoring_guidance.3: Documented customer advisory board or feedback portal; some features attributed to customer input
scoring_guidance.4: Active customer community; product roadmap influenced by customer input; feature voting visible
scoring_guidance.5: Transparent roadmap tied to customer feedback; documented feature request-to-delivery metrics; customer co-development programs

pillars.description: The clarity, quality, creativity and efficacy of marketing programs, and the vendor's differentiated messaging strategy.

sub_pillars.description: Brand recognition in the MDR market, media mentions, social media presence, and overall market visibility.

scoring_guidance.1: Minimal market presence; few media mentions
scoring_guidance.2: Some brand recognition in niche segments; limited media coverage
scoring_guidance.3: Recognized brand in MDR market; regular media coverage; active social presence
scoring_guidance.4: Strong brand with high awareness; frequent media mentions; significant social following; conference keynotes
scoring_guidance.5: Top-of-mind brand in MDR; extensive media presence; industry thought leader status; brand synonymous with MDR

sub_pillars.description: Quality and volume of published content: blogs, whitepapers, research reports, webinars, and educational resources.

scoring_guidance.2: Sparse blog content; occasional white papers
scoring_guidance.3: Regular content cadence; multiple content types; some original research
scoring_guidance.4: Prolific content publisher; own threat research reports; active webinar program; cited by media/analysts
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class content engine; proprietary threat research widely cited; influential blog; annual flagship report

sub_pillars.description: Presence at major industry events (RSA, Black Hat, Gartner SRM, etc.), own-hosted events, and community engagement.

scoring_guidance.2: Attends 1-2 events per year; booth presence only
scoring_guidance.3: Regular presence at major events; some speaking slots; regional events
scoring_guidance.4: Major presence at top-tier events; keynote speakers; own user conference or summit
scoring_guidance.5: Dominant event presence; headline sponsor at RSA/Black Hat; flagship annual conference with 1000+ attendees

sub_pillars.description: Website quality, messaging clarity, value proposition articulation, and digital marketing sophistication.

scoring_guidance.1: Poor website; unclear messaging; no differentiation articulated
scoring_guidance.2: Functional website; basic messaging; value proposition unclear or generic
scoring_guidance.3: Professional website; clear MDR positioning; differentiated messaging; good SEO presence
scoring_guidance.4: Excellent website with strong UX; sharp, differentiated messaging; competitive positioning clear; strong SEO
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class digital presence; industry-defining messaging; website as lead gen engine; omnichannel consistency

pillars.description: Quantitative customer experience metrics that supplement the operational SOG pillar data from the MDR schema.

sub_pillars.description: Aggregated ratings on Gartner Peer Insights, G2, and other peer review platforms. Overall rating, review count, and sentiment.

scoring_guidance.1: No peer reviews found on any platform
scoring_guidance.2: Few reviews (<10); available on 1 platform only
scoring_guidance.3: Moderate review count (10-50); 4.0+/5.0 average; on 2+ platforms
scoring_guidance.4: Strong review presence (50-200); 4.3+/5.0 average; Customers' Choice or similar recognition
scoring_guidance.5: Extensive reviews (200+); 4.5+/5.0 average; Gartner Peer Insights Customers' Choice; G2 Leader

sub_pillars.description: Customer support quality indicators: support tier structure, response time commitments, escalation paths, and satisfaction with support.

scoring_guidance.2: Basic support structure documented; no SLA specifics
scoring_guidance.3: Tiered support with documented SLAs; dedicated account management mentioned
scoring_guidance.4: 24/7 premium support; documented response times; TAM/CSM assignment; high support ratings in reviews
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class support; sub-hour response guarantees; proactive customer success; support NPS published and high

sub_pillars.description: Speed and quality of customer onboarding, deployment assistance, and time to first meaningful detection/response.

scoring_guidance.2: Basic onboarding mentioned; no timeline or process details
scoring_guidance.3: Documented onboarding process with milestones; deployment guides available; reasonable time-to-value
scoring_guidance.4: Fast onboarding (<30 days); structured enablement program; deployment automation; white-glove option
scoring_guidance.5: Same-day or next-day detection capability; fully automated deployment; documented sub-week time-to-value

sub_pillars.description: Evidence of customer success programs, expansion revenue, customer community, and long-term relationship investment.

scoring_guidance.2: Basic account management; no proactive success program
scoring_guidance.3: Designated CSM program; quarterly business reviews documented; customer training available
scoring_guidance.4: Mature customer success with proactive engagement; customer community; documented expansion revenue
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class customer success; customer advisory boards; published NRR >120%; active user community

pillars.mq_criterion_name: Market Understanding + Offering Strategy + Business Model
pillars.description: The vendor's ability to understand buyers' needs, articulate market direction, and align product/business strategy with market evolution.

sub_pillars.description: The vendor's articulated view of where the MDR market is heading, how they define the market, and whether their vision aligns with or shapes market direction.

scoring_guidance.2: Generic market positioning; follows market without clear vision
scoring_guidance.3: Clear MDR market perspective; articulated view of market evolution; some thought leadership
scoring_guidance.4: Strong market vision; shaping market direction in specific areas; forward-looking strategy documented
scoring_guidance.5: Market-defining vision; consistently ahead of market trends; other vendors react to their moves

sub_pillars.description: Published or implied product roadmap, R&D investment indicators, and clarity on future capability development.

scoring_guidance.1: No product roadmap or R&D indicators available
scoring_guidance.2: Vague future direction mentioned; minimal R&D investment signals
scoring_guidance.3: General roadmap themes documented; R&D investment evidenced by hiring and releases
scoring_guidance.4: Detailed roadmap shared with customers; significant R&D investment; patent filings; Labs/research output
scoring_guidance.5: Transparent multi-year roadmap; R&D >20% of revenue; active patent portfolio; research partnerships

sub_pillars.description: Platform extensibility, API marketplace, integration ecosystem depth, and strategy for becoming a platform vs. point solution.

scoring_guidance.1: No platform or ecosystem strategy visible
scoring_guidance.2: Basic integrations; no API documentation; point-solution positioning
scoring_guidance.3: Documented integrations with major SIEM/EDR/cloud; API available; growing partner ecosystem
scoring_guidance.4: Rich integration marketplace (50+); documented APIs with SDKs; technology partner program; platform positioning
scoring_guidance.5: Open platform with 100+ integrations; developer ecosystem; marketplace revenue; platform is industry standard

sub_pillars.description: Clarity and maturity of the vendor's business model: revenue diversification, customer economics, and commercial model sophistication.

scoring_guidance.2: Basic subscription model; single revenue stream; opaque economics
scoring_guidance.3: Clear commercial model; multiple pricing tiers; some revenue diversification
scoring_guidance.4: Mature business model; recurring + services revenue; strong unit economics; documented expansion model
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class commercial model; multiple revenue streams; published unit economics; platform economics emerging

pillars.description: The vendor's strategy to direct resources to meet the needs of individual verticals and geographic regions.

sub_pillars.description: Named vertical/industry solutions, compliance packages, industry-specific detections, and sector expertise.

scoring_guidance.2: Generic compliance mention; no industry-specific solutions
scoring_guidance.3: 2-3 named vertical solutions or compliance packages; industry case studies
scoring_guidance.4: Dedicated vertical offerings for 4+ industries; FedRAMP/HITRUST/PCI certified; vertical GTM teams
scoring_guidance.5: Industry leader in 2+ verticals; deep regulatory compliance suite; vertical advisory boards; industry-specific SOC playbooks

sub_pillars.description: Customer concentration across verticals, published industry references, and vertical market share indicators.

scoring_guidance.2: Customers in 1-2 verticals only
scoring_guidance.3: References across 3-5 verticals; some concentration data available
scoring_guidance.4: Strong presence in 5+ verticals; documented vertical market share in at least one industry
scoring_guidance.5: Dominant in 2+ verticals; comprehensive vertical customer portfolio; recognized as vertical specialist

sub_pillars.description: SOC locations by region, data residency options, regional compliance certifications, and service availability across geographies.

scoring_guidance.2: Primary region plus limited international availability
scoring_guidance.3: Coverage in 2-3 major regions; some data residency options; regional partners
scoring_guidance.4: Global coverage with SOCs in 3+ regions; data residency in US/EU/APAC; regional compliance (GDPR, etc.)
scoring_guidance.5: True global coverage; SOCs in 5+ regions; comprehensive data sovereignty; local language support; regional compliance portfolio

sub_pillars.description: Multi-language support, regional pricing, culturally adapted services, and local partner networks.

scoring_guidance.2: Website in 1-2 additional languages; minimal localization
scoring_guidance.3: Multi-language support (3+); some regional partners; localized documentation
scoring_guidance.4: Comprehensive localization; regional pricing; local partner networks; multi-language SOC support
scoring_guidance.5: Full global localization; local SOC analysts in major regions; regional GTM teams; culturally adapted services

mq_scoring_mode.description: The MQ scoring mode combines existing MDR schema data with MQ Gap research to produce the 15 Magic Quadrant criteria scores. Each MQ criterion has a defined formula mapping source data to a 0-5 score.

criteria.formula: Weighted average of MDR pillar_scores (TDR×0.25, PTI×0.15, ADA×0.05, DIS×0.05, IRA×0.15, AIO×0.15, AID×0.10, SOG×0.10)

criteria.source: MDR pricing + MQ Gap SLE pillar
MDR SOG pillar + MQ Gap CXQ pillar

criteria.formula: (MDR SOG pillar_score × 0.40) + (MDR IRA pillar_score × 0.30) + (MDR TDR-04 SLA score × 0.30)
criteria.source: MDR capability schema — SOG + IRA + TDR-04

criteria.formula: Average of MKE-01 through MKE-04 (shared with ATE-5)

criteria.source: MDR AIO + AID pillars + MQ Gap MKU-02/03
MDR pricing + outcomes + MQ Gap MKU-04

criteria.formula: (MDR AIO pillar × 0.20) + (MDR AID pillar × 0.20) + (MDR ADA pillar × 0.15) + (MDR DIS pillar × 0.10) + (MKU-02 R&D × 0.15) + (MKR-02 competitive response × 0.10) + (MKR-03 M&A × 0.10)
criteria.source: MDR innovation pillars + MQ Gap MKU-02/MKR-02/MKR-03
criteria.gap_supplement: Partial — R&D and M&A research needed

quadrant_placement.description: Final vendor placement uses weighted ATE (Y-axis) and COV (X-axis) composite scores. Quadrant thresholds are calibrated against the vendor population.
quadrant_placement.method: Vendors are placed on a 0-5 scale for each axis. Quadrant boundaries are set at the median of each axis, producing four quadrants relative to the vendor population.
quadrant_placement.challengers: Above median on ATE, below median on COV
quadrant_placement.visionaries: Below median on ATE, above median on COV
